title: Async GPU barrierless collectives and KV-cache shard merging to reduce host-device syncs
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Multi-GPU tensor-parallel inference suffered from unnecessary host-device synchronizations when coordinating collectives and when merging per-shard KV cache updates, causing higher tail latency and lower sustained throughput for short-sequence, low-latency workloads. This PR reduces host involvement in collective handshakes and enables on-device, lock-free merging of KV-cache shards so compute can continue while comms make progress. High-level summary of changes: 1) Introduce an asynchronous progress manager that runs a lightweight device-progress thread per GPU which polls CUDA stream status and drives NCCL progress via ncclCommAbort/async-progress hooks where available, avoiding repeated blocking cudaDeviceSynchronize calls; 2) Implement barrierless collective protocol wrapper that groups operations with ncclGroupStart/ncclGroupEnd and relies on device-side event signaling instead of host-side global barriers; the wrapper exposes the same runtime API but eliminates two forced host synchronizations in the tensor-parallel all-reduce/all-gather paths; 3) Add a KV-cache shard merge path that merges incoming remote shard updates on the device using warp-level primitives and atomic-free double-buffer switching, avoiding host round trips for small shard merges; 4) Scheduler changes: the infer scheduler now tracks outstanding NCCL ops per-GPU and permits compute kernel launches on non-conflicting streams while collectives progress, using per-stream sequence numbers and event fences to ensure correctness; 5) Fallbacks: when platform does not expose async-progress or when NCCL does not support CUDA stream progress, we fall back to previous synchronized path; feature gated via runtime flag --enable-async-collectives; 6) Tests and benchmarks: microbenchmarks for 8xA100 TP-8 runs and end-to-end L32 token generation tests are included showing 18-27% median latency reduction for short sequences and 12-16% increase in sustained tokens/sec in small batch/low-latency regime. Commits summary: commit 1: add async progress manager and scaffolding; commit 2: implement barrierless collective wrapper and unit tests; commit 3: device-side KV-cache shard merge implementation with warp-level merge util; commit 4: scheduler integration and event fencing; commit 5: add feature flag, config, and rollout docs; commit 6: add microbench harness and measurement scripts; commit 7: fixes from review (ordering, extra checks, CI flake fixes). Files changed (high-level): runtime/collectives/async_progress_manager.cc; runtime/collectives/barrierless_wrapper.cc; runtime/collectives/barrierless_wrapper.h; runtime/kv_cache/device_shard_merge.cu; runtime/kv_cache/device_shard_merge.h; runtime/scheduler/stream_fence.rs; runtime/scheduler/stream_fence_tests.rs; examples/bench/async_collectives_bench.py; docs/runbooks/async-collectives.md; integration-tests/tp/kv_merge_e2e.yaml; CI changes to .github/workflows/ci-integration.yml; small changes in runtime/api/collectives.h and runtime/config/flags.cc; tests/unit/collectives_mock_test.cc. Small illustrative snippet: "// in barrierless_wrapper.cc: ncclGroupStart(); ncclAllGather(..., comm); ncclAllReduce(..., comm); ncclGroupEnd(); // host does not synchronize here; device events used for sequencing". Review conversation summary: Reviewer Tomás Rivera: "Huge win for short-seq latencies; major questions on correctness of device-merge under preemption and edge cases where stalled GPUs can block progress. Please add stronger timeouts and clear metrics." Author reply (Aisha): "Added per-op watchdog that triggers fallback to host-synced path after configurable timeout (default 250ms). Added metric runtime.collectives.async_fallback_count and docs describing fallback semantics." Reviewer Evan Li: "Scheduler integration looks sound; ensure stream ordering guarantees across CUDA versions 11.x/12.x." Author reply: "Added compatibility shim and unit tests covering CUDA 11.8 and 12.2; CI matrix updated." Reviewer Priya Sinha: "Tests are extensive but we should be conservative with default flag. Recommend opt-in in 0.1 release." Author: "Flag default is off; rollout doc added with canary thresholds and telemetry checks." CI status and reruns: Initial CI run failed three flaky unit tests in collectives_mock_test due to a race; fixes applied and CI green after two reruns. Performance regressions: none observed on large-batch high-throughput profiles; small improvements measured across all tested TP sizes. Bench numbers: 8xA100 TP-8 small-batch (batch=1, seq=32) median latency down from 24.3ms to 19.7ms; sustained tokens/sec up from 4.1M to 4.6M; CPU utilization down 9-12% due to fewer host syncs. Backwards compatibility and safety: default path unchanged; new code gated by feature flag and runtime config; extensive unit and integration tests added including a mocked preemption scenario; added telemetry metrics for async progress heartbeats, fallback counts, and per-gpu outstanding-ops gauges. Merge notes: squash-and-merge after reviewer approvals; changelog entry added to release notes. Release notes: "Improvement: Async barrierless collectives and on-device KV-cache shard merging reduce host-device syncs, improving short-sequence latency and throughput in tensor-parallel multi-GPU deployments. Feature is opt-in via --enable-async-collectives and guarded by telemetry fallbacks. See docs/runbooks/async-collectives.md for rollout guidance." Breaking change: false.
